tagline.text: Five-level mall by the Marikina River, linked to LRT-2 Santolan Station by a footbridge

location.label: Location
location.text: Calumpang, Marikina City, along Marcos Highway (Marikina–Infanta Highway)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (indoors even in the rainy season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,000 (half day including meals and transport)

children.text: SM City Marikina is the city's flagship shopping mall, opened in September 2008 beside the Marikina River on Marcos Highway. A footbridge links it to LRT-2 Santolan Station, and it sits close to Riverbanks Center in the shoemaking city of Marikina, so it fits easily into a one-day outing.

SM City Marikina is an SM Supermall in Barangay Calumpang, eastern Metro Manila, where the Marikina River meets Marcos Highway. According to Wikipedia it opened on September 5, 2008, sits on a site of about 60,000 sq m with a floor area of roughly 125,000 sq m, and holds more than 400 stores. SM's official page describes it as the 31st SM Supermall built in the Philippines.

The building's structure is its most distinctive feature. The area around the Marikina River often floods during typhoons and heavy rain, so the mall was raised on 246 stilts and its main entrance was placed on the third level. The two lower floors are indoor parking and the three upper floors are retail. First-time visitors can be confused about where to park and which way to enter, but once you understand the layout, getting around is easy. Wikipedia also notes that the building serves as a refuge for residents during calamities.

Access is another strength. Pedestrian overpasses connect the building to LRT-2 Santolan Station and the bus bay, there is a jeepney terminal inside the mall, and an approach road connects directly to the Marcos Highway flyover. It sits on the route from central Manila, Quezon City and Antipolo, so it is easy to stop by on the way. Marikina is known as the center of the Philippine shoe industry, and this mall is the modern face of that city. Along the same river you can find a museum and exhibits on the shoemaking tradition, so you can see the city's heritage by day and relax in the mall in the afternoon. SM's official page describes the mall as the third SM mall opened in eastern Metro Manila. It is close to Riverbanks Center, so the two are easy to visit on the same day.

For travelers, this is less a tourist attraction than an everyday mall where you can shop, eat and rest in one place. Indoors and air-conditioned, you can walk through a food court, restaurants, a cinema, a supermarket and appliance and electronics stores, which makes it a good plan for a hot afternoon or a rainy day. A major expansion and redevelopment is currently under way, however, so the routes through some areas may change because of construction. On a Marikina itinerary, combine it with the shoe museum, Riverbanks Center and the riverside park for a full day. Philippine malls also serve as public places to escape the heat and rain. Watching local families eat out and spend weekends with their children offers a glimpse of urban Philippine life that a sightseeing-focused itinerary rarely shows. Compared with large Korean complexes, the air-conditioning is stronger and the food court plays a bigger role, which makes the comparison fun. Even without a clear shopping goal, it works well as a base for picking up small gifts, lunch and a coffee break all in one stop.

The building stands on 246 stilts and its main entrance is on the third level. It is designed to keep operating even in the rainy season when the Marikina River rises, so it is architecture that shows the terrain and flood history of this city.

A footbridge connects the mall to LRT-2 Santolan Station and the bus bay. You can ride the train from central Manila and walk into the mall without getting wet. Check the latest LRT-2 announcements for operating hours and fares.

The mall gathers The SM Store department store, SM Supermarket and shops for fashion, accessories, books, appliances and household goods. You can see the typical lineup of a large Philippine mall in one place.

blocks.title: Food court and Philippine chain restaurants

children.text: Tenants range from fast food such as Jollibee and McDonald's to chain restaurants such as Max's Restaurant and Teriyaki Boy. It is an easy place to sample Philippine home cooking and Japanese-style chain food, and many families come, so it gets crowded at mealtimes. Many people grab a table first and then order, so if you are with others, have one person keep the seats.

There is a Cyberzone selling smartphones, laptops and game devices, and SM Cinema screens are also available. Check the SM Cinema website for showtimes and whether the cinema is operating on a given date.
The two lower floors are parking, so it is convenient for rental cars and Grab rides. On weekends and paydays the cars pile up, so it is better to arrive a little earlier.

According to the design firm Scott Brownrigg, the project rebuilds the front of the existing mall, adding five retail levels, an atrium and public spaces in phases. We could not confirm a completion date, so check SM announcements before you visit.

Nearby are Riverbanks Center, the Shoe Gallery with the world's largest pair of shoes, the Philippine Science Centrum and the riverside park. After shopping, a visit to see Marikina's shoe culture fits well.

items.title: Half-day course
items.subtitle: Mall browsing, lunch and a riverside walk

children.text: Arrive when the mall opens at

. If you come by LRT-2, you can walk straight in over the Santolan Station footbridge, and if you drive, take the lift or stairs up from the basement parking to the retail floors. Weekend mornings are the quietest.
Browse The SM Store, the fashion shops and the bookstores. If you need cash, look for the ATM locations on the directory boards.
Have lunch at the food court or a chain restaurant. It gets crowded from about 11:30, so it is better to find a seat a little early.
Look around the electronics at Cyberzone or watch a movie. Check the showtimes in advance.
As the sun gets lower, head toward the Marikina riverside and stroll around Riverbanks Center or the riverside park.
The food court can run short of seats at mealtimes, so you could also eat right after opening or after 2:00 PM. While shopping, take a photo of the floor directory so it is easier to get around.
Start with the Marikina Shoe Museum or the shoe shops downtown. Check the museum's opening hours before you go.
Have lunch downtown, then take a tricycle or Grab to SM City Marikina.
Enjoy shopping and a coffee break at the mall.
Have dinner and head home from LRT-2 Santolan Station. Both trains and roads are crowded during rush hour.
Take the LRT-2 line and get off at Santolan Station. Wikipedia says the mall is connected by an overpass.
LRT-2 operating hours and fares can change, so check the latest announcements from the LRT-2 operator.
If you are transferring from the east-west axis of Manila, such as Quiapo or Katipunan, allow plenty of transfer time.
Take Grab or a taxi from Ninoy Aquino International Airport. Travel time varies greatly with traffic, so avoid rush hours.
If your hotel is in central Manila, you can also combine the train and a jeepney.
There is a bus bay and a jeepney terminal near the mall. Check routes and fares on site.
Buses and jeepneys run along Marcos Highway toward Antipolo, Quezon City and Pasig.
The Marcos Highway flyover connects directly to the mall and the underground parking is large.
For Grab, check the pick-up and drop-off zone in front of the mall in the app.

Because it is an indoor mall, you can visit any time of year. The rainy season from June to November is actually good because you can stay out of the rain, but when a typhoon pushes the Marikina River up, it is safer to skip the riverside part.
Crowd-wise, weekday daytime is the quietest, while weekend evenings, the days around payday and the December year-end shopping season are the busiest.

SM City Marikina is the largest shopping facility in Marikina, so the mall itself is where you eat. At the food court you can have Philippine home cooking, grilled chicken with rice and noodle dishes, and there are chains such as Jollibee and McDonald's. Chain restaurants such as Max's Restaurant, known for fried chicken, and Teriyaki Boy, with Japanese-style rice bowls, are good for sitting down as a family. Tenants change often, so check the floor directory.

There is no accommodation inside the mall. Hotels and guesthouses are in downtown Marikina or toward Quezon City, Pasig and Antipolo. If you stay in Marikina, it is a good idea to plan the shoe museum and the riverside together. You can also stay in central Manila and make a day trip by LRT-2 without trouble.

For Korean travelers, browsing the supermarket is a fun part of the trip. At SM Supermarket you can compare and buy souvenir candidates such as Philippine snacks, dried mangoes, coconut products, coffee and sauces in one place. Check prices in the store. After a meal, resting at a cafe to plan the rest of the day and then calling a Grab is the easiest way to finish.
If you come by LRT-2, the Santolan Station footbridge lets you enter without getting rained on. Trains are crowded at rush hour, so avoid it.
If you drive, remember that the main entrance is on the third level, and take a photo of the floor and zone where you parked.
SM's official information lists opening hours as 10:00–21:00 Monday to Thursday and 10:00–22:00 Friday to Sunday. Hours change on holidays and at year-end, so check the latest announcements.
Some entrances and routes may change because of the expansion work, so follow the signs.
It is strongly air-conditioned inside. Bring a thin jacket.
Combining the Marikina Shoe Museum and Riverbanks Center makes for a fuller itinerary.
Many places accept cash, cards and e-wallets, but it varies by shop, so carry a little cash.
SM Supermarket is a good place for souvenirs such as dried mangoes, coconut oil and coffee. Check expiry dates and import rules before you fly home.
Check the locations of restrooms, the nursing room and the customer service desk on the directory at the entrance so you do not get lost.
Many mall entrances check bags, so leave large luggage at your hotel and travel light.
During typhoon season when the Marikina River rises, cut back riverside plans, and check the latest weather information and local government announcements before visiting the mall.
Watch for pickpockets in crowded malls and carry your bag in front of you.
Marcos Highway is extremely congested at rush hour. Leave plenty of time.
Parking and restaurant waits are long on weekends, on paydays and in December.
Opening hours, tenants and movie showtimes can change, so check the official information before you visit.
There may be noise or restricted passage because of the expansion work.
Do not leave your wallet or phone on a table while you step away in the mall.

A complex close to the mall toward the Marikina River, with the Shoe Gallery displaying the world's largest pair of shoes and the Philippine Science Centrum. Check opening hours and admission before you visit.
A museum showing the history of the shoemaking city of Marikina. You can get there from the mall by tricycle or Grab, and you should check opening hours on site.
The area of downtown Marikina where shoe shops and workshops are concentrated.
A large SM shopping mall in Ortigas in central Manila, a good one to compare.
A riverside walking path close to the mall. In the rainy season, check the water level and weather before you go.
